court: In the High Court of Madras
advocates: For Respondent: Mr. I. Abrar Md. Abdullah
prayer: PRAYER: Civil Revision Petition filed under Article 227 of the Constitution of India, against the fair and decreetal order dated 24.09.2019 made in I.A. No. 6041 of 2018 in O.P. No. 2688 of 2018 on the file of the IV Additional Family Court, Chennai.
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

V. Bharathidasan, J.:— With the consent of both parties, Civil Revision Petition is taken up for final disposal at the Admission stage itself.

2. This Civil Revision Petition has been filed to set aside the order passed by the IV Additional Judge, Family Court, Chennai in the application filed by the respondent herein under Order III Rule 2 CPC for appointing his father as his Power of Attorney.

3. According to the petitioner, the respondent/husband has filed a petition in O.P. No. 2688 of 2018 for divorce before the IV Additional Family Court, Chennai. Since the respondent/husband is working as an Assistant Vice President in Bank of America, at USA, he is not able to appear before the Family Court on every hearing, he has given a Power of Attorney to his father Natarajan, and filed a petition to accept the Power of Attorney. The same was objected by the petitioner/wife, on the ground that on several hearing, the respondent/husband has deliberately not appeared before the Court and the Conciliation proceedings has also been not conducted by the Family Court, and, the presence of the respondent/husband is necessary before the Court. The Court below after considering the submissions allowed the application, thereby permitting the respondent/husband to represent through his power of Attorney/father, on all hearings, and permitted him to file any affidavits or counter affidavits on behalf of the respondent. However, the Court below directed the respondent/husband to be present during trial for adducing evidence and subject himself for cross examination of the petitioner/wife and also directed him to appear before the Court as and when required directed by the Court. Now challenging the same, the present revision has been filed.

4. Heard both sides and perused the materials available on records carefully.

5. Admittedly, the respondent/husband is employed in USA and it is not possible for him to appear before the Family Court on all regular hearings. Considering the above circumstances, the Court below rightly held that the respondent/husband can appear through his Power of Attorney and the Family Court further directed the petitioner to be present before the Court during trial for adducing evidence and also cross examination by the petitioner/wife. In the said circumstances, I find no irregularity or illegality in the order Passed by the Court below and I find no merit in the Civil Revision Petition.

6. At this stage, the learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that there is likelyhood of settlement between the parties and the respondent may be directed to appear for the Mediation.

7. But it was opposed by the respondent's counsel, and submits that already a conciliation has taken place and it failed, and there is no chance of any settlement. He further submits the respondent is ready and willing to appear before the Court for giving evidence and also for cross examination by the respondent.

8. Considering the above said circumstances, the IV Additional Family Court, Chennai is directed to dispose the H.M.O.P. No. 2688 of 2018 within a period of four(4) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order on merits and in accordance with law. It is also made clear that the respondent has to appear before the Court and give evidence and also subject himself for cross examination by the petitioner. If the petitioner wants any mediation and conciliation, it can be done during the trial.

9. With the above directions, this Civil Revision Petition is disposed of. No costs.
